morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Start under the leaf and then count style branches: dark-centered stellate hairs make the lower leaf surface look brown-dotted, and the plant has two deeply divided styles (four terminal branches) with a one-seeded fruit.
diagnostic_traits: small annual often branching near the base
dark-centered stellate hairs create brown-dotted abaxial leaf appearance
two styles each bifid to base = four terminal style branches
ovary with only one fertile locule

confusers.separator: C. lindheimerianus lacks the dark-centered brown-dot hairs and has three styles with six terminal segments and a normal three-seeded capsule.
C. texensis is taller, dioecious, narrow-leaved, and has verrucose fruit plus more highly divided styles.
